title: Dataset format and packaging
summary: Turn libphonenumber XML and geocoding files into a compact on-device format
description:
CURRENT STATE: nothing built. Sources inspected and understood: PhoneNumberMetadata.xml (~979 KB, 245 territories, possibleLengths + nationalNumberPattern per country per type) and resources/geocoding (151 countries, 34 languages, 11 MB total, 6.6 MB for English alone).

Build the tooling that converts upstream libphonenumber data into a compact format the core reads directly.

WHY NOT PARSE XML AT RUNTIME: the iOS Call Directory and SMS filter extensions run under tight memory limits. Parsing a megabyte of XML to answer one question is not viable there.

REQUIREMENTS OF THE FORMAT:
- Fast lookup by country and number type; fast longest-prefix match for the geocoder.
- Memory-mappable or lazily loadable, so an extension can answer one question without loading everything.
- Self-describing and versioned, so the engine can run against a dataset it was not compiled against.
- Selective packaging: ship only the countries and languages needed, not all 11 MB. We control this.

DO NOT ASSUME A FIXED SHAPE (Guidelines §1): not every country defines every number type — uan appears in 63 territories, voicemail in 15, of 245. The converter and the reader must both handle types being absent, and must not hardcode the type list.

ALSO CARRIES: R7's UI language files ride the same packaging, so adding a language is not a release.

BUILD IT GENERAL: the format should describe "a versioned dataset", not "phone metadata". R1's daily spam list uses the same format later.

VALIDATION: the converter must verify what it produces — every territory present, patterns compile, prefix tries resolve — because a silently truncated dataset would make rules stop matching with no error.
